title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 11 of 16

questions.question: What is the 'Material-Based Trap'?
options: Mistakenly classifying by function or category, when the true shared property is actually about the material something is made of
A trap only relevant to numbers
A trap with no practical relevance
questions.rationale: This trap involves overlooking that the true shared classification property is the material an item is made from, rather than its function or category.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Use' test?
options: Whether a group of items share a common practical use, with one item having a different use
questions.rationale: This tests whether items share a common practical use or purpose, identifying the item used for something different.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Location' test?
options: Whether a group of items share a common typical location, with one item typically found elsewhere
questions.rationale: This tests whether items share a common typical location, identifying the item that is typically found somewhere different.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Diet' test?
options: Whether a group of animals share a common diet category (herbivore, carnivore, etc.), with one breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether animals share a common diet category, such as all being herbivores, identifying the one with a different diet.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Biological Group' test?
options: Whether a group of organisms share a common broader biological grouping (mammals, reptiles, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether organisms share a common broader biological group, such as all being mammals, identifying the one from a different group.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Taxonomic Level' test, more specifically?
options: Whether a group of biological terms share the same specific level of taxonomic classification (species, genus, family, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether biological terms operate at the same specific taxonomic level (like all being genus names), identifying the one at a different level.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Reproduction' test?
options: Whether a group of organisms share a common reproduction method (e.g., laying eggs vs live birth), with one breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether organisms share a common reproduction method, identifying the one that reproduces differently from the rest of the group.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Physical Property' test?
options: Whether a group of items share a common physical property (density, magnetism, state of matter, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether items share a common physical property, such as density or state of matter, identifying the item that differs physically.

questions.question: What does 'Magnetic Classification' test specifically?
options: Whether a group of materials share the same magnetic property (magnetic or non-magnetic), with one breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether materials share the same magnetic behavior, identifying the one material that behaves differently.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Geometry' test?
options: Whether a group of shapes share a common geometric property (number of sides, symmetry, etc.), with one breaking it
questions.rationale: This tests whether shapes share a common geometric property, such as number of sides, identifying the shape that differs geometrically.
